newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower across the board in spite of increased physical activity. Most active March lost $2.60 to close at $304.40 per tonne, while May gave up $2.30 to close at $303.50 per tonne. In New York heavy fund selling dragged the market to its lowest level in three weeks despite a late round of bargain hunting by the trade. In a fourth consecutive negative close, commodity funds scrambled to liquidate long positions acquired during last week's rally above 11.00 cents/lb. Because of bearish fundamentals funds that were expecting prices to improve may now tend to switch to other commodities. March lost 15 points to close at 10.72 cents/lb, while May ended 11 points lower at 10.83 cents/lb. The deferreds lost between 9 and 10 points.

UKRAINE - According to industry sources beet white sugar production in 1996/97 reached 2.7 million tonnes, down from 3.5 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. Molasses production in 1996/97 was put at 1.1 million tonnes, down from 1.4 million tonnes produced the previous year.

ITALY - Sugar imports in August 1996, the first month of the 1996/97 campaign (August/September) amounted to 20,727 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 19,956 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 379,026 tonnes against 266,279 tonnes in 1994/95 and 218,678 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in August 1996 were France with 4,949 tonnes whites against 9,878 tonnes and Germany with 4,040 tonnes, up from 3,581 tonnes. Sugar exports in August 1996 amounted to 14,198 tonnes, down from last year's 27,124 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 170,210 tonnes against 124,787 tonnes in 1994/95 and 182,179 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in August 1996 were Greece with 4,580 tonnes whites against nil and Lebanon with 2,623 tonnes compared to 2,838 tonnes.

CHINA - Sugar imports in November 1996 amounted to 45,611 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 208,680 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (September/November) up to 328,299 tonnes, sharply down from last year's 777,803 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.944 million tonnes against 2.907 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in September/November 1996 were Australia with 143,058 tonnes raws against 113,881 tonnes, Cuba with 132,590 tonnes, down from 145,953 tonnes and Thailand with 29,382 tonnes, down from 214,498 tonnes. Sugar exports in November 1996 amounted to 25,176 tonnes, down from 92,450 tonnes in November 1995. This brought cumulative exports in September/November 1996 up to 162,609 tonnes, down from 189,325 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 830,203 tonnes against 540,004 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in September/November 1996 were Pakistan with 62,499 tonnes whites against nil, Saudi Arabia with 39,481 tonnes, down from 51,200 tonnes and Hong Kong with 25,228 tonnes against 10,051 tonnes.

TENDERS - Sri Lanka bought 12,500 tonnes of white sugar from Korea's Sam Yong Company Ltd for arrival in Colombo during the second half of February at a price of $338 per tonne c&f. Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) confirmed that an offer by a French company of 13,000 tonnes of white sugar by mistake gave a price of $297 per tonne. Traders said that GEZA also aborted the tender for the purchase of 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar because the price which also was given by mistake was very high. It is expected that GEZA will issue another tender within a week to replace this one. The original tender issued on December 14, called for bids for 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws for delivery in February. Iran is thought to have bought one cargo of white sugar at $318 per tonne. Traders said there is a chance Iraq may announce another tender as part of its oil-for-food deal.
